title: Stan Kroenke's New Mexico Land Purchase Makes Him Largest Private Landowner in U.S. - NY News Daily
text:
Stan Kroenke, the billionaire owner of the Los Angeles Rams and Denver Nuggets, has made headlines once again—not for a sports victory, but for a staggering land acquisition that has redefined his status in the United States.
Billionaire Stan Kroenke became the country’s largest landowner with a 937,000 acre purchase In December, Kroenke, 78, completed the purchase of a sprawling 937,000-acre ranch in New Mexico, catapulting him from the fourth-largest private landowner in the country to the top spot.
This move has not only upstaged California’s Lumber Dynasty, the Emmerson family, who previously held the title, but has also set a new benchmark for land acquisitions in the United States.
According to Fox2, the sheer scale of this purchase has made it the largest single land transaction in the country since 2011.
The New York Times and the Santa Fe New Mexican have both highlighted the significance of the deal, noting that the ranch spans four counties in New Mexico and constitutes approximately 1.2 percent of the state’s total land area.
Kroenke owns several sports teams including the Arsenal soccer club in the United Kingdom Despite the massive size of the acquisition, the exact price of the land remains undisclosed, adding an air of mystery to the deal.
Kroenke’s new acquisition is just one piece of a vast puzzle that includes over 2.7 million acres of land across North America and 60 million square feet of commercial real estate.
His land portfolio, which now includes the previously Teledyne-owned ranch in New Mexico, is a testament to his long-standing interest in large-scale land ownership.
This is not his first foray into such acquisitions; in 2016, Kroenke made headlines by purchasing the Waggoner Ranch in Texas, the largest ranch in the state at the time.
His ranch portfolio included the larges in Texas, the Waggoner Ranch That 535,000-acre property, which hadn’t changed hands since 1849, was reportedly valued at over $500 million.
The Waggoner Ranch, now part of Kroenke’s growing empire, is just one of many properties that span across Texas, Montana, Wyoming, and Nevada.
According to the Land Report, Kroenke uses his extensive land holdings for a variety of purposes, including cattle ranching, hunting, wildlife habitat preservation, and even renewable energy initiatives.
His ranches are not just personal retreats but also serve as economic and environmental assets, though the implications of such large-scale land ownership on local communities and ecosystems remain a topic of discussion.
Beyond his ranches, Kroenke’s influence extends into the commercial real estate sector.
His portfolio includes sports facilities in Inglewood, California, and Denver, as well as ownership of several major sports teams in the United States, including the Los Angeles Rams, the Denver Nuggets, the Colorado Avalanche, and the Colorado Rapids.
His ventures are not limited to the U.S.—he is also the owner of the Arsenal men’s and women’s soccer clubs in the United Kingdom, further cementing his global presence in sports.
His real estate holdings are equally impressive, with one of his most notable properties being a $25 million Malibu mansion once owned by Dodi Fayed, the lover of Princess Diana.
This eclectic mix of assets underscores Kroenke’s ability to diversify his investments across multiple sectors, from sports to real estate to land management.
Kroenke’s financial success is reflected in his estimated net worth of $26.8 billion, as reported by Bloomberg.
This wealth has been built through a combination of strategic real estate deals, sports team ownership, and other business ventures.
Born in Missouri, Kroenke married Ann Walton Kroenke, the heiress to the Walmart fortune, which has further bolstered his financial standing.
His journey from a businessman to one of the wealthiest individuals in the world has been marked by a series of high-profile acquisitions and investments.
According to Forbes, Kroenke ranks 47th on the list of the world’s wealthiest people and is recognized as the ninth richest U.S. sports team owner.
His success is not just a personal achievement but also a reflection of the broader trends in private land ownership and corporate influence in the United States.
When compared to other high-profile billionaires, Kroenke’s land holdings are in a league of their own.
Jeff Bezos, the founder of Amazon, reportedly owns 462,000 acres, while Bill Gates, the co-founder of Microsoft, has only 275,000 acres.
Kroenke’s 937,000-acre acquisition in New Mexico alone surpasses both of these figures, highlighting the sheer scale of his land portfolio.
This level of land ownership raises questions about the role of private individuals in shaping the American landscape and the potential impact on public land use policies.
As the largest private landowner in the United States, Kroenke’s influence extends far beyond his personal wealth, touching on issues of environmental conservation, agricultural practices, and even the potential for future government regulations aimed at managing such large-scale private holdings.
While the details of his new ranch and its management remain largely private, the sheer magnitude of his land acquisition underscores the growing trend of billionaires amassing vast tracts of land, a phenomenon that will likely continue to shape the economic and regulatory landscape of the United States for years to come.
